p1_strategy_write_owner_cas_replay.defect: ports/strategy_write_owner.py update_entry's command_key replay check compared a subset merge (committed_entry.metadata updated in place with the incoming record) against the committed metadata, so a same-key retry that genuinely omitted a field the original request carried (e.g. description) left that field untouched by dict.update() and was silently accepted as an idempotent no-op with a different response, instead of being rejected. It also always re-read entry.metadata fresh as the CAS expected_metadata for the non-replay path.
p1_strategy_write_owner_cas_replay.fix: Replaced the subset/dict.update() comparison with an exact-equality comparison against the receipt's frozen committed_entry.metadata: a candidate metadata dict is recomputed the same way a real commit would (record verbatim, only the registry-internal versions/current_spec_version_id bookkeeping keys backfilled from a stable source when the caller never supplied them at all) and compared for exact dict equality against committed_entry.metadata. Equal -> genuine idempotent replay, return without a second write. Not equal -> RegistryConflictError, matching the canonical Registry's own reject-different-intent semantics. The first-application (no existing receipt) path is unchanged: expected_metadata is still the entry's freshly read current metadata, required for the real CAS in PostgresRegistryStore.commit_metadata_cas.
p1_strategy_write_owner_cas_replay.why_not_reading_entry_metadata_fresh_for: commit_metadata_cas's own request_digest binds (expected_metadata, new_metadata); recomputing expected_metadata fresh at replay time necessarily differs from the original commit's precondition whenever an unrelated command_key mutated the row in between, which the store then treats as a divergent replay (reviewer finding 6 in split_api.py/pg_store.py) even though the intent is identical. Comparing the write owner's own candidate metadata against the frozen receipt short-circuits before ever calling commit_metadata_cas for a genuine replay, so this drift never reaches the digest at all -- and a genuine intent divergence (a caller-omitted field) is still caught, because it fails the new owner-side exact-equality check before the call would ever be made.
